# Treeix

> Treeix is a free, open source (Apache 2.0) AI workspace for Mac and Linux. Your AI workspace: everything you use daily, in one app. Agent terminals run in a background daemon and keep going when you quit the app. Treeix shows what each AI coding agent (Claude Code, Codex or any CLI agent) changed in its worktree, and sends your line comments back to the agent session as its next prompt. Pull requests, tickets, a chat view and a browser pane sit in the same window.

AI agents write code faster than anyone can read it. The reading is the bottleneck, and it is usually spread across a terminal, a git client, a browser tab per pull request and a tracker. Treeix puts one worktree, its diff, the review comments, the pull request and the agent session that produced it on a single screen.

- Platform: macOS 13.3 or later as one universal build for Apple silicon and Intel, signed and notarized by Apple. Linux: an x86_64 AppImage on GitHub releases. A built-in updater. Dictation and meeting recording need Apple silicon. A native app: Rust and Tauri, with a React interface.
- Price: free. No account, no telemetry, no Treeix server.
- License: Apache 2.0. Source: https://github.com/zaxovaiko/treeix
- Works with: Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, any shell or CLI agent, GitHub (gh), GitLab (glab), Jira (Atlassian CLI, acli), Notion (personal access token). Each integration is optional.
- Made by Dyvertex (https://dyvertex.com), a software house that builds and rescues web apps.

## How it works

1. Pick a worktree: every repository and worktree shows up in one sidebar, with a count of changed files and the diff against the base branch, split or unified.
2. Drag across the lines that need another pass and write a note. Notes keep the file and the line range and wait in a drawer.
3. Send the queue: the notes go to the Claude Code or Codex session running in that worktree as its next prompt. Only references are sent, the code itself is not copied into the prompt.

## Features

- Sessions that keep running: the treeix-ptyd daemon owns every shell and agent session. Quit Treeix, open it again, and each one is still there with its scrollback. Sidebar or horizontal tabs, recursive splits, sessions grouped by repo and worktree, a quick terminal on a global shortcut, and notifications. A status dot on Claude Code and Codex sessions says working, waiting for you or done.
- Worktrees and review: an Explorer and Changes with split or unified diffs. Line comments queue in a drawer and go to the Claude Code or Codex session in that worktree as its next prompt.
- Session history: closed sessions stay in History; reopening one resumes the same agent conversation.
- Open worktree: start from a branch, a pull request or a ticket from Your tickets, and copy the .env files across.
- Pull requests panel for GitHub and GitLab through gh and glab: list, check out, open, merge, and CI checks.
- Tickets: Jira through acli and Notion through a personal access token. Both are off until switched on in Settings.
- Routines: an agent run on a schedule, on a GitHub or Jira event, or on a local webhook (127.0.0.1 only). They run in the repo, in a fresh worktree or in the pull request's worktree, with a turn budget and permissions. The daemon runs them, so they fire with Treeix closed. Each routine picks its result: local commits, a draft pull request, or a push to the pull request it worked on. Treeix commits, pushes and opens the pull request after a clean run; agents never get push or pull request tools.
- Chat view for Claude and Codex next to the terminal, kept across restarts. It needs npx.
- Phone: Settings, Phone serves a mobile page to your own Tailscale network, answered only for your Tailscale login. Answer agents that need you, type into terminals, reply in chats, run or switch routines and open the pull requests they made. Served by the daemon, so it works with Treeix closed.
- Race: one prompt to several agents, a worktree each.
- MCP server: agents can open files, panes and worktrees in Treeix, and drive the browser pane.
- Browser pane: built on the system WebView instead of Chromium, with a console and network view. An error can go to the agent in one click. Agents can open pages, read them, click, type and take screenshots; Settings has a switch for that.
- Plans: Claude Code's plans as a pane, with mermaid diagrams and line comments.
- Module graph: a repo's packages and the imports between them, with import cycles and unresolved imports marked.
- Editor and search: a Monaco editor with diffs, find in files and file history.
- Ports: the ports your sessions listen on, with open in the browser pane and kill.
- Usage limits: Claude and Codex 5-hour and weekly limits in the title bar, and tokens per agent, model and project in its popover.
- Dictation (off by default, Apple silicon): hold a hotkey, speak, and the text lands at the cursor. Recognised on the Mac.
- Meeting recording (off by default, Apple silicon): record a call into a transcript and a note, on the Mac.
- Command palette for commands, worktrees, sessions, files, pull requests and settings.
- Themes: 14 dark and 8 light, after Vercel, Claude, Apple, Xcode, VS Code, GitHub, Solarized, Nord and Dracula.
- Keeps the machine awake while an agent works.
- Most features can be switched off in Settings; a feature that is off does no work.

## FAQ

- Does my code leave my machine? Not through Treeix. It runs git, gh, glab, claude and codex locally and has no server. What you type into an agent goes to that agent's vendor, as in your own terminal.
- Which agents does it work with? Claude Code and Codex, in a terminal pane or as a chat, with a status dot. Other CLI agents run in a plain shell session.
- What happens when I quit Treeix? Shells and agent sessions keep running in the treeix-ptyd daemon and reattach with their scrollback when you reopen it. Routines fire with Treeix closed.
- Do I have to use git worktrees? No. A plain repository or a plain folder works. Worktrees make one agent per branch easy.
- What do I need installed? Git. Optional: gh or glab for pull requests, claude or codex for agent sessions, acli for Jira, npx for the chat view. Notion takes a personal access token.
- Which systems does it run on? macOS 13.3 or later (Apple silicon and Intel) and Linux x86_64 (AppImage).
- Is it free? Yes, free to download and open source under Apache 2.0.

## Roadmap

- Sessions on your other machines over Tailscale and SSH, in the same sidebar.
- A design pass over every screen.
- A Windows build.
- Contributions are welcome, see https://github.com/zaxovaiko/treeix/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md
